content.intended_use: Resolve dimension and accuracy dependence under globally strongly convex higher-order operator-norm smoothness and fresh noisy scalar values.

dependencies: Same Source: Lemmas 4.1-4.2, C.1-C.2, Proposition D.1, Lemmas D.2-D.3; their interfaces and source-linked arguments are recorded here.

Imported mathematical interfaces: chain rule for relative entropy, Gaussian equal-variance KL, Pinsker inequality, divergence theorem (fundamental theorem of calculus for d=1), Euclidean projection nonexpansiveness and convexity. These are not separate claims of reading cited external papers.
map: A and Lemma 4.1: differentiating chi(||w||^2) over partitions into singleton/pair blocks bounds derivative operator norms independently of d; bounded kth and (k+1)st derivatives give global alpha-Holder control.

B and Lemma 4.2: shared radial cutoff perturbs ||x||^2 by -a h^beta F_{s/sqrt(d)}(x/h). Hessian lies between I and 3I; kth increment scales as a H_beta ||x-y||^alpha; minimizer is (a/2)h^(beta-1)s/sqrt(d).

C.1: for all x the sum over flipped-sign squared signals is at most 4a^2h^(2beta)/d. Conditional Gaussian KL chain rule, with the same action kernels and seed under both instances, gives mean edge KL at most 2a^2 T h^(2beta)/d^2.

C.2: pair opposite decisions on each hypercube edge, apply Pinsker and Jensen to obtain mean Hamming error >=d(1-sqrt(Kbar/2))/2. Setting h=min{1,(d^2/(16a^2T))^(1/(2beta))} yields Kbar<=1/8 and mean Hamming error >=3d/8. Sign errors and strong convexity yield average objective gap >=3a^2h^(2beta-2)/64, hence the saturated lower rate.

D.4: sphere/ball smoothing identity, vector Taylor remainder controlled by scalar multilinear operator norm through Euclidean duality, and Lagrange cancellation yield bias <=B_beta h^(beta-1). Fresh independent noise across scales yields second moment <=V_beta d^2/h^2.

D.5 and D.2: weighted projected SGD yields gap <=B_beta^2 h^(2beta-2)+4V_beta d^2/((n+1)h^2). For T>=2q d^2, n=floor(T/(2q))>=d^2 and n>=T/(4q), h=(d^2/n)^(1/(2beta)). Otherwise return 0, whose loss <=3/2; saturation absorbs this branch into C_beta.

proofs.full_local_argument: Write p=(beta-1)/beta. Choose epsilon_beta>0 with epsilon_beta<c_beta and epsilon_beta<=C_beta. If E_beta(T,d)<=epsilon<=epsilon_beta, then c_beta min{1,(d^2/T)^p}<=epsilon<c_beta. Thus the minimum cannot be 1, and T>=d^2(c_beta/epsilon)^(1/p). Conversely T=ceil(d^2(C_beta/epsilon)^(1/p)) gives the upper risk <=epsilon. The quantity inside the ceiling is >=1, so the ceiling is at most twice that quantity. Constants therefore depend only on beta, uniformly in d and the stated epsilon range.

assumptions: Euclidean R^d; all class inequalities are global, with constants independent of d,T and epsilon.
Oracle returns Y_t=f(z_t)+xi_t with fresh iid standard Gaussian xi_t, independent of algorithm randomness; evaluations at two points have independent noises.

Algorithms are measurable adaptive strategies using at most the fixed integer budget T on every run, with arbitrary computation, memory and independent randomization; z_t and final xhat may be anywhere in R^d.
statement.conclusion: c_beta min{1,(d^2/T)^p} <= E_beta(T,d) <= C_beta min{1,(d^2/T)^p}, p=(beta-1)/beta. Q*_beta(d,epsilon)=Theta_beta(d^2 epsilon^(-beta/(beta-1))) for 0<epsilon<=epsilon_beta, with no logarithmic loss. Upper witness queries only in B_2^d(2) and uses 2q values per gradient iteration, q=1+floor((k-1)/2); small budgets return 0.
statement.objects_and_definitions: For fixed finite real beta>2, k=ceil(beta)-1, alpha=beta-k in (0,1], p=(beta-1)/beta. F_beta(d) consists of f:R^d->R in C^k, with unique global minimizer x* in the closed Euclidean unit ball, and for every x,y in R^d: f(y)>=f(x)+<grad f(x),y-x>+||y-x||^2/2; ||grad f(x)-grad f(y)||<=3||x-y||; ||D^k f(x)-D^k f(y)||_op<=||x-y||^alpha. The operator norm is sup |A[u1,...,uk]| over independently chosen unit-ball directions. Define E_beta(T,d)=inf_{A using at most T raw calls} sup_{f in F_beta(d)} E_f[f(xhat)-f(x*)]. Define Q*_beta(d,epsilon)=inf{T in N:E_beta(T,d)<=epsilon}.
statement.parameter_domains: d,T positive integers; beta fixed finite >2; accuracy assertion restricted to sufficiently small positive epsilon depending on beta.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every fixed finite beta>2 there exist 0<c_beta<=C_beta<infinity, independent of d,T, such that for every integer d,T>=1 the two-sided minimax inequality holds. Equivalently the lower bound means every admissible randomized adaptive algorithm has some fixed f causing that expected loss. Expectation covers observation and algorithm randomness. There exists epsilon_beta>0 such that for all d>=1 and 0<epsilon<=epsilon_beta the query-complexity assertion holds.
